messages.author: 8be372cf55f0d085
messages.subject: Sem - Perfect fit -
parts:
Dear all,

I am new in performing SEM.
The model I am using for my model is quit simple:
model<-'EA ~ Guseful+intention + socialnorms +reliable+emoji'

All variables used are observed ordinal variables (scale 1 to 5). And the estimator used is DWLS.

I am asking your help regarding the results associated to my fit that are perfect:
  • The Comparative Fit Index (CFI) and Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI) are both at 1.000,
  • The Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) and Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR) are both at 0.000.
I am skeptical regarding this output, and I was wondering if it is due to my very simple model, or if it might be due to different issues...

If someone could provide me with some information, it would be perfect,
Kind regards,
Louis

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Sem - Perfect fit -
parts:
Your model is saturated.  You are estimating all of the parameters that you can, and so there are no degrees of freedom left. 

This is a regression model, and it is expected behavior.

Try doing something like:

EA ~ Guseful + intention + 0 * socialnorms + reliable + emoji

You've added a constraint, and so the model will have 1 df. The p-value associated with this new model should be very close to the p-value of the parameter estimate that you removed in the first model.

Jeremy

messages.subject: Re: Sem - Perfect fit -
parts:
I am not the OP but I would like to ask a related question.

I noticed that Louis used DWLS. Put aside whether DWLS is the most appropriate method in this case (all variables ordinal variables with five possible responses), is it acceptable to use SEM solely as an estimation method? That is, we intentionally fit a saturated model just to estimate the parameters using methods available in SEM.

In my personal tentative opinion, this is totally fine to fit a saturated model. Certainly, in this case, we cannot focus on model fit because the fit is perfect a priori. However, we can still legitimately talk about the parameter estimates. However, I rarely see researchers in my area doing this.

-- Shu Fai

messages.subject: Re: Sem - Perfect fit -
parts:
Shu Fai--
Then you can have your debate about estimators. If the ordinal data issue were not present, then you might have the OLS people making an argument about precision of estimators for given n and plausibility of distributional assumptions. But with ordinality, even though DWLS is only an approximate solution, I don't know what the OLS counter-argument would be--maybe estimating regression coefficients from polychoric correlations with bootstrapped standard errors (?).
This is assuming that the saturated model is believed to be "correct."
--Ed R.
